records.text: # The first morning the setup pays back.Threshold (entry) · the seeding flow’s landing · design settled 2026-07-07

The threshold the operator hits on entry — the moment the app “rises up to greet” them and hands back the one move. Welcome is where the seeding flow lands: after setup the workspace is already deep (ICP + accounts + ≥10 deals + quota), so this is never an empty on-ramp — it is the first morning the hard work reads itself back.Sourced from: canon §4.1 + the heavy-seeding doctrine (§12) + the seeding flow (§4.3). Settled design: welcome-flow-landing-2026-07-07.html.

## What the room is forClose the loop the onboarding doorway opened — “do the hard work once, the system reads your motion back to you every morning” — and make that playback the whole room. One commanding statement, one dominant move (the system’s top pick, read overnight across the entire workspace), and the payback shown as a quiet secondary read. Progress is felt as becoming operational, never gamified, no finish line.2 · What it offers

The commanding statement | One serif line that names the state — day-one landing (“the workspace is awake”) vs re-entry (“what moved since you left”). The only thing that changes between the two lifecycles. |

The one dominant move | The system’s single overnight pick + its plain reason + one CTA. The system read the whole workspace while the operator was away; this is the one thing that needs them first. |
The “what the system saw” read | 2–4 plain lines — the dividend on the setup work. Never a checklist, never a status dump. What the system noticed on its own. |
The operating line | A recessive read: accounts watched · live deals · in flight. The “morning door” into the workspace — never “all done.” |
The calm route to the Dashboard | A quiet, non-competing path to the full command surface for the operator who wants more than the one move. | 3 · The two lifecycles

## One layout, two headlinesDay-one landing and re-entry reuse the exact same shape; only the headline changes. This is the whole trick of the room — the payback surface is identical whether it’s the first morning or the hundredth.
Lifecycle | Headline register | What the read says |
Day-one landing | “The workspace is awake — here’s what you just switched on.” | the first move + what the seeding produced |
Re-entry | “What moved since you left.” | account/deal movement since last session + the one move | 4 · Flows
directional handoff into the room that owns the one move — Signal Console / Deal Workspace / Outbound
Welcome as the seeding flow’s landing — never an empty-workspace “create your first…” threshold
the payback made visible (“what the system saw while you were away”)

# The one ranked object under the most pressure — and the one move.Command Chamber (ranking) · settled 2026-07-04

Show the operator the single ranked object under the most pressure right now, with one dominant next move, without browsing. The Dashboard is where the operator stops choosing between modules and starts being told which deal, signal, or pilot to act on first — it ranks everything under pressure, explains why a specific object came up first, and offers one compressed act-or-inspect move.Sourced from: canon §4.2 + the command-intelligence engine (Part V · buildCommandObjects / rankCommandObjects / summarizeCommandContext / explainCommandObject). Settled design: dashboard-CHOSEN-complete-2026-07-04.html.

## What the room is forReplace the hallway (equal-weight doors) with a smarter front door: one ranked object, one dominant move, the reasoning shown. Three density modes support different cognitive states; all three keep the ranking. This is the room the whole system’s workspace-health summaries flow into. Supersession (2026-07-08, founder-confirmed): the settled 2026-07-04 "command + standing cockpit" folds the three cognitive states into one surface (standing = the Brief read · the one move = Spotlight · skip-the-board = Queue), so there is no explicit mode switcher, and the "this week's reads" card is not carried on the Dashboard. Sections 2 + the "this week's reads" row below are retained as history.2 · The three density modes
Brief | A 2–5 sentence narrative read + one variable-insight line | wants the morning read in prose, then the one move |
Queue | A ranked triage list — rank prefix + reason chips per row | wants to work down the pressure list one at a time | 3 · What it offers
The ranked object list | Everything under pressure, ranked — deals, signals, pilots, moves, the ICP itself, system reads. |
The Brief narrative | A deterministic morning read (buildBriefNarrative) naming the spotlight, the queue composition, the ranking confidence, the runner-up. |
The ranking inputs (shown, never hidden) | how hot the signals are on an account · how much pressure a deal is under · how stale · dollar value · what changes downstream if you act. |

# Could a real first-hire walk in tomorrow and run the motion?System Ledger (synthesis) · design settled 2026-07-07 (the climb)

Answer one question — is the system inheritable yet? — and give the operator a verdict, not a number. Readiness is a maturity assessment, not a pressure rail: an integral over time, not a derivative. The Dashboard already answers “what should I act on today?”; Future Autopsy answers “what’s decaying?”; Readiness answers “is the workspace inheritable yet?”Sourced from: canon §4.17 + the readiness engine (verdict.ts · dimensions.ts · dashboard readiness-aggregator). Settled design: readiness-score-climb-2026-07-07.html.
You are the system | Founder-led, no transferable surface yet | any part at 0 |
Building | Activity exists but a hire would still be improvising | ≥2 parts ≥8, none ≥16 |
Inheritable with guardrails | A hire could run it with you there to answer questions | every part ≥10 AND ≥1 part ≥16 AND first pilot evidence exists |
Hire-ready | The motion would survive a 2-week founder vacation | every part ≥14 AND closed-won exists AND Future Autopsy run AND ≥1 actionable pilot |
Hire-ready, repeatable | Multiple wins, losses analyzed, advisors lit, kit composed | all Hire-ready + win/loss ≥1 AND advisors ≥1 AND handoff ≥5/7 ready | 3 · What it offers
The verdict | The dominant serif state name + a plain one-line read of what a hire could / couldn’t do today. |

The climb (the ladder over time) | The five levels as a vertical ladder — passed levels sit behind in forest green (“left behind 3 weeks ago”), the current level is “you are here,” the next is the goal + “what it takes.” |

The five parts of the motion | Demoted to quiet ready/thin chips (forest = solid, amber = thin) — your targeting · your outreach · your discovery · your open deals · your pilot evidence. Never bars, never scores. |
The read-only “share with a hire” | The one durable move — read-mode workspace access for an external email. |
Ceremony hooks | Fires the Founding GTM set-piece on a verdict transition UP. | 4 · Flows
Future Autopsy run history
a verdict transition UP fires the ceremony moment in Founding GTM

# The one sharp definition of who you sell to.Decision Bench (strategic shaping) · settled 2026-07-04

Sharpen the one definition of who you sell to so every downstream room can work against a real target. The ICP object is the thing being sharpened — it is the central authored surface, not a form output. Thin means fewer assumptions, fewer personas, fewer use cases. The ICP is the filter that manifests as “ICP Match” scoring on every Account, everywhere.Sourced from: canon §4.4 + the ICP build + 8-check quality engine (shipped src/icp-studio). Settled design: icp-studio-combo-flow-2026-07-04.html.

## What the room is forMake one sharp ICP the filter the whole system runs against. The ICP is a strategic bet the operator authors, not a persona template they fill. Every account, everywhere, carries an ICP-Match score derived from this one definition.2 · What it offers
The buying-group minimum | The smallest real buying group the motion needs. |
The focus recommendation | The system’s read of where to sharpen — narrower beats broader. |
The 8-check quality engine | A 4-tier read on how sharp the ICP is (thinness rewarded, not penalized). | 3 · Flows
ICP sharpness as a strategic bet
# The ICP, carved into a territory you actually own.Decision Bench (strategic shaping) · settled 2026-07-04 (axis-morphing floor)

Turn the ICP into a tiered territory with focuses, approaches, and a hard 300-account ceiling that forces strategic ownership. The territory is a map of focused groups of buyers, not a list. A focus is a named division of the market, carved on whatever axis fits the motion — and the axes blend.Sourced from: canon §4.5 (carve-axis malleability + why-you/why-now charter, 2026-07-03) + shipped src/territory-architect. Settled design: territory-architect-axis-morph-2026-07-04.html.

## What the room is forCarve the ICP into divisions the seller can actually own. The carve axis is a variable, not a constant — the room stays malleable from a scorch-the-earth pre-seed (one coarse division) to an organized Series B (a geo × vertical grid). The 300-cap + swap make each account consequential; tiers are a resource-allocation commitment, not a ranking.2 · The carve axes
Trigger / behavior | pressure charters |
Why-now (what pressure is on them) | required for trigger carves · optional-but-encouraged for structural carves |
Sales-cycle calibration | Tunes the territory to the motion’s cycle length. |
The carve axis | geo / vertical / segment / named / trigger — blendable; sets the room’s register. |
Axis-malleability (never hardcode one carve)

Find accounts, confirm each one is real and worth it, and send only the confirmed ones to Signal Console. Keep the funnel moving — never a filing cabinet. Antaeus runs its own web research: the operator describes who they want in plain language, and Antaeus reads public news, funding announcements, job posts and company pages, and brings back companies that match — each cited with a link.Sourced from: canon §4.6 (the search mind-correction, 2026-07-03) + shipped src/sourcing-workbench. Settled design: prospecting-desk-funnel-2026-07-04.html (variant F1: Find → Confirm → Send).
Saved searches + auto-watches | run-on-demand searches the operator triggers + watches Antaeus re-runs on its own and alerts on — with a productivity read + a dry-search flag. |

The room where the operator tracks the named accounts they’re watching, the signals attached to each, and the next move on each. Accounts come in by hand or from enrichment; signals stack up against them; the operator decides what to act on. Signals are time-limited events — research on a qualified account may justify motion, but research without motion is collection theater.Sourced from: canon §4.7 + the heat engine (shipped src/signal-console) + ADR-006 (substrate role). Settled design: signal-console-attention-router-2026-07-04.html.

## What the room is forRank the watched field by where attention should go. Account heat feeds Dashboard command ranking. Post-ADR-006 the room is also the data substrate the Briefing reads from — accounts + signals live in the signal_console_accounts + signals Postgres tables this room owns. The Briefing reads; it never writes back.2 · The heat engine
Heat = signal count × type weight × source credibility × recency decay
Heat score per account | The computed rank (above) — feeds Dashboard command ranking. |
The morning brief | The daily read on the watched field. |
Research posture | “motion ready” vs “research heavy” — guards against collection theater. |
The enrich-all flow | Pull enrichment (triggers / firmographics / heat) across the field. |

# What the system saw — inside your work and out in the market.Intelligence Surface (new family, closest neighbor System Ledger) · named premium asset · ADR-006

The daily check-in for what the system saw — both inside the operator’s own work (the Workspace stream) and in the market the operator is selling into (the World stream). Written like a peer telling them what they see. Not “what to act on next” (the Dashboard’s job) and not “which accounts are on the radar” (Signal Console’s job).Sourced from: canon §4.21 + ADR-006 + ADR-009 + ADR-014 + the 13 promoted specs (deliverables/specs/briefing). Settled design: briefing-vivid-2026-07-04.html.

## What the room is forBe the daily check-in for what the system saw. The operator’s stated preferences (watchlist, ICP, competitive set) are treated as hypotheses under continuous evaluation, not fixed truths to serve. A responsive product accepts them as given; the Briefing tests them continuously and tells the operator when the evidence isn’t supporting the hypothesis.2 · The two streams
Workspace | the operator’s own deals / signals / pilots (the ADR-009 ledger) | daily-fresh · SQL heartbeat generators |
Pattern | a synthesized read: claim + evidence + confidence + audit envelope. |
## What comes in, what goes outThe Briefing is the intelligence surface that reads from the Signal Console substrate (accounts + signals + heat in Postgres). It never writes to those tables.Flows in

## What the room is forTurn the operator rack (account · buyer · persona · temperature · trigger · next-question) into the exact spoken/written line — a real, specific outbound move, never template spam. The generator maps 5 temperatures × 4 personas to a send line + a quality read + a motion band.2 · What it offers
Quality + motion band | ready ≥80 / workable ≥60 / thin — is the line real enough to send. | 3 · Flows

# LinkedIn as disciplined air cover — never the opening scene.Live Instrument (live execution) · settled 2026-07-06 (the one move)

Use LinkedIn as disciplined air cover — never the opening scene. Public cue first, ask only when trust has compounded. The inbox is not where you start: the five cues run watch public signal → comment with one operating read → connect after recognition → give-first → ask only when it’s warranted.Sourced from: canon §4.10 + the motion engine + 5-cue ladder (shipped src/linkedin-playbook). Settled design: linkedin-playbook-one-move-2026-07-06.html.

Surface the recovery queue — which deals are weakest, why, and what the next corrective move is. The room is an intervention board, not a Kanban. First-fold exposes pressure fast: which deals will close-lost if I do nothing this week, and what’s the smallest corrective move. # The deal isn’t won when they say yes.Live Instrument (live execution) · renamed from Negotiation 2026-07-07 · settled (face-off + ledger)

Get a verbally-agreed deal actually signed — walk the seller through every front between “we want to buy” and a countersigned contract, push back where they should push back, and keep the buying committee engaged so the deal doesn’t die in procurement. The most common way a B2B deal dies is not losing the argument — it’s internal alignment collapse after the verbal yes.Sourced from: canon §4.16b (the run-to-signed reconceive + rename, 2026-07-07) + B2B procurement research (SIG/CAIQ · SOC 2/ISO shortcut · liability caps · MAP). Settled design: getting-to-signed-faceoff-2026-07-07.html.

## What the room is forA war room for the run to signed, not a rehearsal booth. It leads with the one thing actually blocking right now (the biggest gap between their ask and your line), shown as a face-off — their side ⟷ the gap ⟷ your line — with the seller’s counter, a trade they can offer, and the line they won’t cross. Everything else open sits below as a positions ledger.2 · The four disciplines
## One ledger row each; the hottest is the face-offThe room morphs which front is the face-off by what’s actually blocking, not a fixed order.
Front | What it covers |
The committee | champion / economic buyer / new stakeholders, each with an engagement read (warm / quiet N days / new). |
The face-off | their side · the gap · your line + hold/trade/line + “send the counter-position” + “loop in an advisor who’s won this fight.” |
The positions ledger | per-front row: their ask → your line → status (blocking / clearing / to-do / at-risk); each row drills to its depth in place. |
The payment-terms trade set | net-60 flat · net-30 for a cut · % off for annual up-front. |
The plan-to-signed | the mutual dated run to signature, co-owned with the champion. |

The living onboarding surface the first hire opens on day one — where the founder’s tacit GTM memory becomes a transferable artifact. Not an export; the workspace itself is the durable artifact post cloud-sync. The kit’s job is authored opinion + cross-room synthesis, not aggregation — it renders the founder’s hard-won understanding as prescriptive, surprising, specific content the hire can read top-to-bottom.Sourced from: canon §4.19 + the section authoring engines (src/founding-gtm/lib/sections.ts + cross-room.ts). Settled design: founding-gtm-open-book-2026-07-07.html.

## What the room is forDo what the workspace cannot: render the founder’s GTM understanding as prescriptive, surprising, specific content. Specificity comes from authored opinion (not bullet aggregation) and from cross-room reads no single room could surface alone. This is the culmination — every other room points toward getting the workspace ready to hand off.2 · The seven sections

## Each authored, each with a cross-room “one thing to notice”Replacing the legacy six. Each section is authored prose + a concrete evidence line + one cross-room read (the “surprise” primitive in code; renders as a plain “one thing to notice” margin note, never labeled “SURPRISE”).
Seven authored sections | Prose that reads like a document a sharp operator wrote for their replacement — not aggregated bullet lists. |
Per-section status | ready / partial / empty — shown honestly, thin parts not hidden. |
The per-section cross-room read | The “one thing to notice” — the read no single room can surface alone. |
The share-link mechanic | Read-mode workspace access for an external email — the one durable move. |
The ceremony hook | Fires the set-piece on the first upward Readiness transition into Inheritable-with-guardrails. | 4 · The ceremony moment

## The kit becomes realWhen Readiness transitions UP from Building → Inheritable with guardrails for the first time in a workspace, fire a set-piece (not a toast): an animated reveal — the verdict change, the kit count moving (e.g. 2/7 → 4/7), a serif headline (“the kit just became real”), and a one-time CTA to share the workspace read-mode. Once per workspace per upward transition; downward transitions are silent.5 · Flows
